svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.9.8.5 Exiting through a Lobby
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.9.8.5 Exiting through a Lobby
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.9 MEANS OF EGRESS
Exiting through a Lobby

g.text: Only one exit from a floor area above or
below the first storey may lead through a lobby
Lobby 4.5 m max. above grade, path
through it to the outdoors 15 m max.
Other rooms may open onto it, but not

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Not more than one exit from a floor area above or
below the first storey is permitted to lead
through a lobby
The lobby is not more than 4.5 m (14′-9⅛″) above
grade, and the path of travel through it to the
outdoors does not exceed 15 m (49′-2½″)
The lobby conforms in all respects to the
requirements for exits
Except that rooms other than service rooms, storage
rooms and rooms of residential or industrial
occupancy are permitted to open directly onto it.
Where the lobby and the adjacent occupancies
permitted to open into it are sprinklered, the
fire separation between them need not have a
fire-resistance rating
Note A-3.4.4.2.(2)(e): a lobby that an exit leads
through must provide a level of protection
approaching that of the exit.
Passenger elevators are permitted to open onto
the lobby, provided the elevator doors are
designed to remain closed except while loading
and unloading passengers
Drawn: the first storey, walls cut low. Gold: the lobby. Pink walls: separations of the lobby and exits.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.9.8.5. (page 9-53), with Note A-3.4.4.2.(2)(e).
